growth_garp_v2.asks: Growing fast at a fair price: sales up at least 10% a year, earning at least 12% on its capital, and not overpaying for that growth (its price no more than twice its growth rate), for companies worth at least $5bn.
growth_garp_v2.asset_kind_rationale: Revenue CAGR, ROIC and EBIT/EV describe an operating company, not a fund; an ETF scored on look-through vendor fundamentals is quiet garbage, so it is gated out.
growth_garp_v2.description: Growth at a Reasonable Price: rank durable compounders on revenue growth, capital efficiency (ROIC), valuation (earnings yield) and 12-month momentum, over names that pass the growth screen (revenue CAGR, ROIC, PEG, mid/large cap). Momentum is a rank factor, not a screen gate (v2): dip names rank low, they are not vetoed.
growth_garp_v2.name: Growth at a Reasonable Price
growth_garp_v2.rationale: Great businesses compound revenue at high incremental returns on capital; the discipline is refusing to overpay for that growth. Ranking survivors of the growth screen on growth + quality + valuation + trend orders them without tuned weights, the same rank-sum mechanic the value strategies use. Momentum drags dip names down the order; it does not gate them out.

growth_garp_v3.asks: Growing faster than most of its industry at a fair price: a BUY needs sales growth above the industry median; names are then ranked on sales growth, return on capital, price and trend, among profitable, growing companies worth at least $5bn.
growth_garp_v3.asset_kind_rationale: Revenue CAGR, ROIC and EBIT/EV describe an operating company, not a fund; an ETF scored on look-through vendor fundamentals is quiet garbage, so it is gated out.
growth_garp_v3.description: Growth v3: rank profitable, growing companies worth at least $5bn on revenue growth, capital efficiency (ROIC), valuation (earnings yield) and 12-month momentum; a BUY additionally requires revenue growth in the top half of the ranked set (buy_requires), otherwise the name is HOLD with the reason shown.
growth_garp_v3.name: Growth at a Reasonable Price
growth_garp_v3.rationale: Great businesses compound revenue at high incremental returns on capital. v2 asked for that with three absolute thresholds and a price test, which left too few names to judge. v3 keeps the scope broad (profitable, growing, $5bn+), ranks on the same four factors, and puts the growth demand where it belongs: a relative one. "Growing faster than most of its industry" is a statement about the group, so it is a cap on the BUY, not an absolute rate.
growth_garp_v3.sector_exclusion_rationale: Revenue growth and return on capital do not measure a bank or an insurer: deposits, loans and premiums are the business.

growth_screen_v2.description: Capital-efficient growth (revenue CAGR + ROIC) bought at a reasonable price (PEG), scoped to mid/large caps — the screen lens for a Growth-at-a-Reasonable-Price rank candidate. Momentum is NOT a gate here (v2): dip names are dragged down by the momentum_12m rank factor, not vetoed by the screen.
growth_screen_v2.name: Growth screen
growth_screen_v2.rationale: Great businesses compound revenue at high incremental returns on capital; the discipline is refusing to overpay for it. Revenue CAGR evidences the compounding, ROIC that the growth creates value, and PEG keeps valuation honest. Momentum is expressed as a rank factor in the strategy, not a screen gate — a dip name ranks low, it is not screened out.

growth_screen_v3.description: Profitable, growing companies worth at least $5bn: three absolute floors and nothing relative. The scope definition for the Growth v3 rank candidate; the relative judgement (growing faster than most of the industry) lives in that strategy's BUY cap.
growth_screen_v3.name: Growth screen
growth_screen_v3.rationale: Scope, not selection: a business that is growing and earns something on its capital is in the room; the ranking decides who is best in it. Keeping the floors absolute leaves enough names in each industry group to be ranked and judged at all.
